claims.claim: Reviewers report performance issues including frame rate stutters and game crashes.

citations.review_text: crash out many times, game looks so bad.

Gameplay was alright, similar to dungeon crawlers like Minecraft Dungeons except it has a shoulder camera instead of top down.

Main deal breaker for me was the long dialogue (especially in the tutorial), unintuitive controls on keyboard and bloated ui menus. 

Oh, and the stutters. I have an ok pc, and I should be able to run this game just fine, and for a few minutes of gameplay i was getting 80fps in the 99th percentile. But then it dropped of a cliff, and I kept bouncing around 20 to 100 fps, sometimes when Im just standing there. Messing with the settings didn't fix it.

claims.claim: The game lacks built-in key binding options to change controller layouts.

citations.review_text: The inability to change the control bindings makes this one practically unplayable, at least for me. Every other similar game uses B for dodge, so that's what I'm used to. If I use Steam Input to change it, then I have to mentally reverse what A and B do in menus, and I have even stronger, older, muscle memory to try and go against for that. Then, when I play other games, I'll be backwards there. Being able to change bindings is mandatory for the vast majority of games. I really don't understand wtf designers and/or developers are thinking when they don't provide that feature. It's not because the game is old at this point. This was a completely known and understood issue at that time. Another problem with using Steam Input is that glyphs don't match, and that's also a problem that has an impact when you switch to playing a different game.

Graphics bug out a lot, surface looks worse than played on a cellphone. And every game i need to hack files to make it work ain't worth spit, even on sale.
It's a grindfest with boring monsters until the first boss - that is, what a surprise:
a nuisance with a frequent spam of buggy spawning exploders.
Last game for a long time i bought on steam, all these controller-games hastily made to work on a pc are just never cutting it for me. And every game where you need multiple players to continue soloing ain't my game.
Maybe i'll play past it if i ever fall ill for a month - can't see that one coming though.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that boss encounters involve fighting additional standard enemies alongside the boss.

citations.review_text: I bounced off this on console when it released. Revisited this recently on PC, currently playing in VR (UEVR). Very fun game given it's age. Gun play is solid. Some complaints are overused environments and dungeons that feel the same. My largest complaint has to be the additional and continuous spawns during boss fights. Pretty much every boss has these and it makes the fights frustrating and tedious. They corrected this in Remnant II, but be aware this is present in the original. Still a fun game though.

You ever play a game and think of an older console generation in a good way? That's this. This is all the benefits of the 360/ps3 era of games with none of the problems. Its a third person shooter with souls like elements. The difficulty feels fun without ever feeling absurd. The most annoying element in my opinion is that like 99% of the bosses have additional enemies attacking you. Not even like unique enemies its just the standard enemies from the area. Its annoying till you realize because you rely on guns instead of melee weapons; the bosses can't rely on things like input reading in the same ways you've seen before. Them ignoring hit-stun never made me roll my eyes cuz I'm not point blank when they do it. It doesn't matter if they delay their attacks. Think of every cheap arcade final-boss style mechanic or design choice Fromsoft gives its bosses. For example, my personal least favorite is them hitting the ground and it effects my health bar. In this game stuff like that doesn't work because.... You have a gun, a gun imbued with varying magic albitites. THE GUN ITSELF CAN BE SCIFI BS. So the bosses behave differently and they absolutely have to. There were a couple bosses I didn't like because their gimmicks were kind of annoying for example one was authentically harder in coop than solo because of the nature of what the boss was doing. No spoilers but it involved bullet-hell/stage hazard elements that were triggered by the boss in response to our positions in the boss arena. Hence 1 person easier to avoid. Regardless of all that this does what every souls like game I like does well and that gives me an array of weapons, that aren't lame, relatively quickly. Nothing will ever top bloodborne the only game like this where I can say I LIKE EVERY WEAPON. This is close though. Like two of the weapons I found were crossbows I typically hate crossbows and they were still mad fun. Last good crossbow in videogames was the first Bioshock. I highly recommend this game es…

super good game, reminds me of dark souls and gears of war with a slight dishonored aesthetic. the bosses are kind of cheap by spawning in smaller enemies to kill you but not terrible beat 80 percent of it without once playing multiplayer but having 2 others really made it significantlly better for collecting loot as you can split off and search different areas.

claims.claim: Joining online sessions can result in the loss of personal campaign progression upon returning to a solo game.

citations.review_text:
The gameplay is fine. It starts to feel repetitive. 

Worst part of this game is that I join a online match with someone at the same spot as I was.. played for 7 hours and got to Founder Ford.... and game stopped letting me input anything or move. 

When i reset and went back into my game, I had 0 progression in my own storyline even though my experience and weapons progressed.. That seriously killed the game for me.

Fun game TBH, i got it for free on epic games some 5 years ago now probably. I remember i put it down after just two hours on EG, frustrated at the lack of clear indication where i needed to go to progress. At 10 hours in, i can say that i still feel the same way AT TIMES, and if not for randoms happening to join my game and show me where to go, i probably still wouldnt know. At one point, randoms joined my game and we ran for 50 minutes in circles trying to find the dungeon we needed, because the game simply just doesnt directly tell you and you have to figure it out on your own. In that time frame, we acquired many gear supplies, which are simply just useless after you upgrade your gear to a certain level, requiring nomatter what the next tier / zones supplies instead. makes no sense why they even drop at a certain point in general. That being said, the gameplay is pretty solid, the combat itself is pretty fluid, the character and boss designs are fairly cool and theirs a host of cosmetics to choose from, granted they can be grindy to unlock. All of those missing features of where to go, coupled in with the fact that their is no chat or way to communicate with other players directly aisde from waypoint markers, i cant really say i would recommend it overall to someone who doesnt have 8$ to just blow, or 12 for the complete edition.
Edit: forgot to mention, being that the game is so old, its not exactly uncommon for max level / gear players to join your game and team kill either. If you are host you can ban them from your game, but most people seemingly have no idea how to kick them, and since theirs no text or voice comms....yeah, self explanatory. just a lot of BS to deal with for one game tbqh.

Remnant is a really fun horror co-op game, especially when playing with friends. The gameplay is excellent, the shooting feels great, and the graphics are absolutely outstanding. The boss fights are one of the best parts of the game, and the story is also really good.

I first tried playing solo, but I struggled a little with some of the adventure and puzzle sections. Puzzles and exploration are not really my type of gameplay. My biggest issue was the lack of a proper map. The game sometimes tells you where you need to go, but it does not clearly show the location on the map, so you have to figure it out yourself. Because of that, I got stuck a few times while playing solo.

However, playing with friends was a completely different experience. I had a lot of fun and finished the game with my friends in around 8–9 hours. Even after finishing the main game, there is still grinding and farming that players can do, especially in multiplayer.

For me, this game is much more enjoyable with friends. If you have a few friends to play with, I definitely recommend giving it a try. The shooting, bosses, graphics, story, and co-op gameplay make it a really enjoyable experience.

This is my personal review and my personal experience with the game. My English is not very good, so I am using ChatGPT to help me write this review in English, but the opinions and experiences in this review are completely my own.

Short and sweet PVE shooter, and every random that joined was a really chill individual who would point out little hidden secrets and just kinda vibe until it was time to go shoot things. Did get a little lost for no good reason a few times, but that might be a skill issue.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the maps and world layouts as randomized or procedurally generated, requiring players to reroll areas to find specific items, events, or bosses.

citations.review_text:
An excellent TPS strong soulslike influences and a real identity of its own. The boss fights are varied and satisfying, progression feels rewarding, and the difficulty is demanding without becoming unnecessarily frustrating. Co-op makes the experience even better.

100% Completion
Time : 77.3H
Completion Difficulty : 6/10
Playthroughs : 1+
Missables : Yes
DLC Required : Yes
Notable requirements : Complete the main campaign, replaying/rerolling worlds because the bosses and events are randomized, defeat 10 bosses consecutively in survival mode.

I went into Remnant: From the Ashes knowing almost nothing about it besides hearing that it was a pretty good game, and I’m honestly glad I kept it that way. I ended up having an absolute blast and was completely hooked for nearly 60 hours.

The story was great, the bosses were memorable, and the twists and turns kept me interested all the way through. The gameplay is easily one of the strongest parts of the game. The gunplay feels great, character building is satisfying, and there are tons of weapons, armor, traits, and items to experiment with when putting together different builds.

I also really enjoyed the way the game handles exploration and farming. The RNG elements, different map layouts, random encounters, bosses, and unique items that can appear during different runs give you a real reason to replay areas instead of everything feeling exactly the same every time. Hunting down rare gear and figuring out the different ways certain items can be obtained added a lot to the experience for me.

The multiplayer was also a lot of fun and worked really well with the overall design of the game.

By the time I finished the main story, defeated the final boss, and played through the DLC, I had nearly 60 hours in the game and felt like I absolutely got my money’s worth.

Overall, Remnant: From the Ashes was a great experience that completely surprised me. I had an awesome time from beginning to end, and now I’m genuinely excited to jump into Remnant II.

Gonna give this a mixed review but leaning towards negative.  The game is....fine, but that's it.  I think it's a fantastic base but I just wish there was *more* to it.

Remnant does a poor job of explaining to the player that the maps are semi-random and that you will miss out on events and bosses unless you roll an adventure or second campaign.  Well this mechanic is interesting I just found it tedious because the semi-random maps are comprised of several of the same pieces just different orders or with 1 piece exchanged for another.  You'll quickly recognize layouts, enemy placement, turns, and loot locations.  What doesn't help this is the medium speed at which you run through these levels making it feel like a chore.  If you want a specific event, boss, or piece of equipment you have to hope that RNG was on your side or else you have to reroll the adventure and go through the maps again...and again....and again...with the same enemy placements, the same layouts, the same bosses, the same mechanics.  It's dull.

The story is...there, somewhere.  At first I was interested but early on I was given a 12 page journal with mostly filler written by a character I didn't care about and I tuned out after that.  I don't know why souls-like games love their vague, indirect storytelling so much and Remnant is especially bad about it.

The visuals are really nice, the world design is cool, there's good build variety, and I did find myself excited whenever I got a unique weapon to check out how it felt to use.  The gunplay is satisfying and I never got bored of it, and the material grind is better than I expected it to be.

All in all I'd say get on sale, it's just okay.

Good 3rd person shooter with very good combat.
The game is mainly running through linear maps to dungeons where you fight a boss and eventually find a final boss of the area. Areas are randomly generated and can have different bosses when you reroll an area. The progression is very soulslike except that traits replace stats and you find new traits as you play.
The rng in bosses and dunegons adds tons of replayability but the lack of dungeon tile variety really shows after a couple runs. The final area bosses usually have alternate kills that give you different items so you want to retry bosses at least once.
Unfortunately there is no way to choose the events, dungeons or end bosses in an area and you may have to reroll a lot which sucks, especially in the swamp dlc.
Get it bundled on sale with the dlc, both add good content. subject for more campaign and a new area. Swamp if you can put up with rerolling for "cut" content and the best boss.

Got it's quirks but really solid, and even with it's quirks/issues it is super addicting. Interesting lore which I am still learning and processing, and cool designs. Hope 3 comes out at some point, here is hoping.  Had this in my log for a while, got a hankering to try it, and then didn't stop. 

The art direction is really solid mixture of a few styles. 
The game is not a one playthrough game though, while it can be, it is primarily styled in multiple playthroughs as many things are randomized, like events, and bosses, and some items. Very secret heavy style too, ever think to talk to an old man for a while? Well maybe you should. Notice a weird locked door, it can be opened, and there will be a way to as long as you get the right spawns. Puzzles and secrets galore, but it's nice you can reroll worlds as then you can look for all the secrets and items within them, instead of fully relying on full playthroughs.

I really, really, really enjoy this game. The only souls-like about it are the checkpoints. It's more of a dungeon shooter. 
The best part of it I think it's the whole campaign is random from a set of dungeons and bosses, so your experience is different from mine, and there's a game mode that let's you visit those missions or bosses that you missed in your main campaign. 
The way you level up is also unique, you get traits that you can level up depending on what you do in game, it doesn't feel like you are wasting level ups on useless things that you don't use.

There's also different rewards for bosses. you get different loot depending on how you kill a boss. 
I think a big downside is that you cannot explore different weapons easily, you might get to upgrade 2 weapons all the way. BUT there are mods (Double Drop Quantity on Nexus) that can give you more drops if you want to upgrade without worrying about sticking to one or two guns. 

Play on Hard, it makes it more entertaining if you like "dark souls difficulty." 

People complain about the story, but c'mon it does it's job. You don't need a deep story for a game like this.

This is a difficulty review, and another clear candidate for a "Neutral" rating option.

On one hand, GunSouls is an interesting take on the genre, and the gunplay and in combat movement feels solid and is fun.  The weapons are all shockingly well balanced, and you can build around anything from the start gear to full end game gear and have great success.  They all feel distinct, and change how you play, too, so it's not a case of being balanced by being bland.  The armour, too.  So overall, the gear and game play is really rock solid.

The problem I have is in the presentation, for want of a better word.  I hate how this game is put together.  When you start new game, it randomly generates the world - so on a given playthrough, you might not even encounter certain bosses (and therefore miss their boss weapons, mods or armour), and quests might not be completable, you might have the quest item but the end point just doesn't exist in your world.  You can reroll the world to have new items, bosses, dungeons etc, but you still have no guarantee of what you'll get until you either grind out a bunch of playthroughs or use external third party tools that were clearly developed because others hated this system as much as I do.  It adds so much unnecessary grind while also adding absolutely nothing of benefit to the player.  I'm not sure why they chose to do things this way, either?  Surely it can't be a dev time related limit, because building the procedural system must have taken as much dev time as just building an overworld with a few more dungeon entrances?

The game also lacks clear communication - at the start you have to pick a class, but are given absolutely no information on what this actually means.  You can pick up the stuff you get later, but it changes your early game run and you have to do it blind.  I could easily see someone picking something that doesn't gel with them and just putting the game down thinking it sucks.  Finally, base movement is woeful…

Remnant: From the Ashes is an awesome "Souls-like" co-op game, in an 3rd person perspective. It is completely randomnized but its feels still good. The highlight of this game are the boss fights. The Abillity Perks are fairly rudimentary. :x

Buuuut, i recoomend it, because it's very fun with friends and mostly fun as a solo-player.

Really great shooter with fun boss fights and dungeons.

Getting new gear feels rewarding and there's tons of different builds that you can go for. Playing solo or with friends works well and you can enable your game so random players can join to your current story progression or you can others.

I've also played Remnant 2 and which is better is personal opinion imo, both are great.

One bad thing is that the randomized maps and layouts and the whole dungeon system is quite confusing before you understand how it works and how to progress in linear sense.

9/10, we need more PVE MP/COOP games!

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a limited selection of available weapons and armor sets.

citations.review_text:
Dark soul with guns, emphasis more on dark soul than guns. The guns don't have customization or myriad of varieties, but limited mods that basically cast magical spell. The weren't bombastic but it work for the game's  need. At the very least it not toy-ish like current Borderlands guns nowadays.

There is sense of generic-ness on the gameplay experience but for 1st time playing while it's fresh, It does good on what it offers. The landscape varieties does hook me on the immersion & enemy is fun to engage. The slow tempo of play really took me to blame for my lack of skill as it maintain my dopamine. Failing to beat a boss can feel like the zen of calmness I wish to indulge forever.

I hate that our base don't have immersion when we progress with the story. The place is exactly the same from beginning to the end of story, as if we contribute nothing. There is few different dialogue line & the addition of mother root character, that's it. There is no other base with different community. Also the end of story with andrew ford is lacking. Really the guy can escape anytime as there is no guards at his place. It's like he is wallowing on his own guilt & don't want to be found. He deserve a smack.

There is a mod for harder difficulty with new boss. I may try it later but for now I recommend this game.

Full disclosure, I started a playthrough alone and completed it alongside two friends. Don’t play this game alone, it feels like it was made with the purpose of playing with one or two friends. Had I played it alone, I might’ve dropped the score down to a three from a four but we’ll get into that in some of the other sections.

Don’t get me wrong, I like the game, and I stand by my 4 out of 5 rating, but I do think it’s somewhat neutered. Build-crafting feels disparate, you’ll spend a good chunk of your first playthrough using the same items that you’ve gotten accustomed to and poured the most resources into as armor sets are hard to come by, most rings and amulets seem like they need some sort of counterpart to really make them shine. New weapons and weapon mods will come as drops from bosses and mini-bosses, and while I do think this system is engaging and rewarding gameplay wise, I did feel that the majority of weapons and mods went right into the bin with a shrug.

Oh cool, a level five hive cannon, let me try it out for a little while. Ten minutes later I’m switching back to my level ten pistol. It’s a shame because the weapon design, plus the way some mods alter the weapon design is so damn cool! You’ll get slightly more mods than weapons from boss fights and I really can’t say I cared too much for them. After each fight we’d hurriedly run back to the crafter and wait our turn to talk to her (crazy this game has multiplayer but players have to talk to crafters one at a time btw), only to find to find some mediocre mod, shrug, and then toss it over our shoulders. Nice, yet another mod that summons some sort of beast to fight beside us for a period of time, daring today, aren’t we?

And this isn’t ubiquitous, of course, but I struggle to see a reason as to why someone would use a new mod or weapon or armor set unless it’s objectively better or you just seem to have the crafting resources burning a hole through your pocket to level every new item up to a fair lev…

Great game, god tier. The only gripe I have is the lack of weapons and armor, especially armor. Literally, the best armor for ranged damage is the starting set that  I have (which is super ugly). Everything else is incredible.

At first, I didn’t have high hopes for it, but as I progressed, I found myself getting more and more hooked on the story. I played it in coop with a friend and I have to say it was a blast. Friendly fire was funny too, though I did take a bullet to the back at some pretty bad moments more than once.

Even though the bosses are sometimes recycled as elite enemies later on, that doesn't take away from the incredible work put into each of them. It felt like playing Dark Souls but with guns XD. Excellent game.

It's a great game, but it has its flaws: there are very few weapons and even fewer armor sets; the bosses are entertaining and varied, but their difficulty seems a bit random; there are plenty of unlockable perks, but few are actually useful; and finally, the NPCs don't react at all to what you do. Still, it's worth it—and even more so in co-op (Friendly Fire was hilarious XD). It's a solid Souls-like with guns.

citations.review_text: Sewers HP and enemy density too high. Some boss fights are very BS RNG when solo.

[b] Only play this multiplayer. [/b] 

The game designed with multiplayer, so if you play it singleplayer like me you're not gonna have the best experience. For instance most bosses will have a bunch of minions that are just frustrating when palying alone. 
The maps and objectives are sometimes confusing for me.

About the final boss of the base game.
[spoiler] The base game has the literal worst final boss I've ever seen, Its a two stage fight with two unskippable cutscenes that repeat if you die. The boss mechanics for the second stage are also not clear atall, I had to look them up. The boss initialy gives the impression that it has an insane amount of health but aparantly you have to wait a bit get transported and then kill minions to stock up a buff specifc to this fight that boosts your damage against the boss, then you have to break this shield like state first after wich you can damage the bosses weakspot properly. Tip just use two summon abillities on your weapons and the soul link ring, it makes the second stage a joke. [/spoiler]

Surprisingly I did enjoy the game alot inspite of everything and can see how nearly all of my problems with it would be solved by just playing it in co-op. So if you can get a friend onboard I highly recomend you give this a shot.

About the DLC.
[spoiler] So to play the DLC story you have to seemingly delete your main story progress and vise versa. The DLC also adds an annoying frostbity status effect which just leaves you stun locked, naturaly there is a boss that is pretty much guaranteed to put this effect on you. Also the final boss of the DLC has pretty much the same problems I had with the one from the base game, exept the cutscenes are skipable now. However the DLC one has a significantly longer run back and you have to interect with this weird stone thing to enter a alternate reality so you can use the portal to go to the boss instead of the snow area, which I had to look up since it is poorly conveyed to say the least.…

It's honestly a good FPS game! Loved the upgrades, weapons and the pure chaos of clearing waves, fighting bosses and shooting your hearts out (I miss this type of game). Plus, you can do multiplayer! 

The thing that I found frustrating is that some of the bosses are not good for solo players. Their mechanics are focused on team fights - spawning hordes of enemies and multiple continuous AOE attacks. You will be able to beat them, but it will take multiple tries/upgrades.

The story though is just basic but I would still recommend this game as I had fun playing!

(Also, I bought it during sale!)

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features challenging and demanding boss fights that can be punishing, particularly for solo players, but become more manageable and enjoyable when played in co-op with friends.

citations.review_text: This game has become one of my all-time favorites. I’ve played Elden Ring and tried Dark Souls, and this game has a similar feel to them. The addition of guns makes it a bit more exciting, in my opinion. There are a few minor bugs, but overall, the game is incredibly fun to play. If you’re having , trouble  find a buddy to play with and help you along the way, don’t worry. There are plenty of options of players who will spawn and help you if you wish.

This game (and Remnant 2 even more)  a masterpiece. While the game is "souls-like", most of the time you don't have problems with enemies and you can progress perfectly. Some big boss is really hard or kind-of impossible to beat alone, but with at least one person could help to go through that fight. When I played alone some part I've allowed other players to join so we could beat the boss which I had issue with. I played through the game with a friend as well and playing again now with an another. While Remnant 2 have much better skill system, this one still feels perfect to play with. Even after Remnant 2 I don't feel bad to recommend this game at all. Buy this game, and if you like what you get buy the second as well. I recommend all DLC included. While the game story is close to nothing the world still feels interesting enough to go around. I strongly recommend this game. I've tried only 1-2 soul-like game before but those felt dry while this felt interesting.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game includes an adventure mode and a hardcore or permadeath mode.

citations.review_text:
This game is an underrated gem! I cannot believe how good this game is! I would honestly say this is probably the best third person shooter I have ever played. The story is a nice original take on their own universe and I didn't find fault in its conception or writing. The controls are tight, the shooting is tight, the movement and the dodge roll/neutral dodge are crisp and responsive, just how you want it. The gameplay is challenging, rewarding and addicting as hell! The game runs flawlessly for me, better than many contemporary triple A games and I believe the environments are quite nice to look at. The audio is good, you'll get audio cues before attacks are made (great for off screen attacks) which is a great immersive/gameplay feature. As for the music I turned that off after my first completion and just listened to techno while slaying. The amount of build variety in the game is substantial and the game offers an excellent amount of variety for replayability with difficulty settings, adventure mode (letting you engage with bosses you never even encountered in your campaign) and hardcore and survival mode (I will talk more about the latter below). I had beaten the game multiple times with my friends and at least twice solo (normal and hard) and got all the achievements. I love this game.

I would like to take some time to give a word of advice to my fellow completionists... Like me, if you are soloing the "Dominator" achievement, I would HIGHLY suggest that you attempt solo play, or in fact, start tackling survival mode's "Beat 10 bosses in a row in survival mode" achievement as soon as you can/early on in your time with this game. Predominantly my time spent in the game was with two of my friends. Majority of the time I was in a squad of 2-3 tackling the many bosses this game offers. This, unbeknownst to myself at the time, was a HUMONGOUS crutch and in no way shape or form prepared me for solo survival mode. At the time of writing this I had just accomplished …

you don't need to play this before remnant 2, but you should. its a great game on its own and it will make you appreciate how they expanded on the series in remnant 2. this one also has a rogue-lite mode (that i put more time into than the main game) if thats your thing. worth.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game features procedural generation for its worlds and levels.

citations.review_text:
I love this game. It is a game of adventure with lots of loot and combat. It is called Dark souls with guns but other than campfire esque checkpoints there are many differences. The worlds are randomized making the routes a little different each time with the blocks that make the worlds recognizable once you play it a ton. 

The combat is smooth as butter with two guns and a melee weapon that are easy to switch between. The weapons are varying in both playstyle and effects with extra modifiers available to add extra power to your build. Your character also has access to a necklaces and rings that have a wild variety of effects. The game can be played both as a min-max type of bulid crafting while also being played with a random assortment of gear you initially get, not efficient but it works and you are alive so it is fine.

THIS GAME IS MEANT TO BE PLAYED MULTIPLE TIMES. Some bosses have multiple rewards and conditions making a single playthrough of this game only like 30% of the whole loot you can get. This can be frustrating to some but it was so fun for me to play through the game again on a harder difficulty and try out many different builds while getting new loot for more builds.

The story is interesting yet is also a bit bare bones to be honest. It could have been fleshed out more but overall it gives enough of a structure to make the gameplay flow.

Playing this game with others is a whole lot of fun and allows for more build variety as you run and gun through enemies. Solo is actually where I put in most of my hours though and it is possible to beat everything in the game solo on the hardest difficulty.

The bosses are one of the funner parts of the game as they test certain builds/skills as you have to figure out ways to deal with them even if you don't have an optimized build. In this game they can be a little dependent on additional chump enemies as the main source of ammo for the player through the fight, but most are manageable and some don't even hav…

A Fantastic Experience!
​I really enjoyed this game. While the story is average and not very gripping, the gameplay is incredibly fun and addictive. Even though there aren't many regions, the procedural generation makes every run feel fresh—bosses change, and they drop different materials for weapons and armor, so it never feels repetitive. Playing in co-op is even better since your friend's world will be different from yours.
​The only downside is the DLCs; I wouldn't recommend buying them unless you are a completionist aiming for that 100% "Perfect Game" status on Steam. Other than that, the base game is a must-play!
